I was going to write a well-thought out review to this game, but since it's Borderlands, here's a list of enemies whose designers I sincerely hope never find gainful employment in the video games industry ever again.

Rakks: Flying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that frequently get stuck inside your hitbox, causing the game to register millions of damage, instantly depleting your shield and putting you at 10% HP.

Buzzards: Tanky flying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that move around like they're being piloted by someone that's simultaneously drunk and on crack. Way too much HP, way too hard to hit, and spawn way too often.

Surveryors: Flying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (are you seeing a theme here?) that also move around like their AI is being piloted by someone that's simultaneously drunk and on crack. Shoots electrical bolts at you that deplete your shields before flying away to Tanzania for approximately 3 business days.

Stalkers: The developer that thought giving a small, hypermobile, hard to hit mob, access to invisibility that it spams quite literally every 0.2 seconds needs a psychiatric evaluation.

Loaders (of all kinds): Extremely tanky. Take 3 steps in any Hyperion-controlled territory and you're going to get assaulted by at least a dozen of these. Their weak point is literally a single red dot on their chassis that is absurdly difficult to hit, and even worse, some variants (BUL Loaders and Power Loaders) cover their weak spots.

Rats: Extremely erratic movement makes it almost impossible to land clean headshots on them. They also steal your loot and hit like an absolute truck for no reason. Also has a fun habit of running away whenever you get close and digging into the ground to escape.

Threshers: Whack-a-mole, except the moles can lob highly damaging projectiles at you, burrow into the ground the second you even think about approaching them or have them within your crosshairs, and some can even hit you from under your feet by sending burrowing tentacles.

Marauders: Simple foot soldiers that seem harmless until you get downed into FFYL mode. When that happens, they immediately bolt away to Uganda in order to deny you second wind. Also I swear their AI makes it so that the moment you have them in your crosshairs, they'll duck under cover for approximately 8 hours.

Nomads: So tanky and for why? Tiny head hitbox makes aiming for headshots on these guys absolutely miserable. Also why do they move around like that despite being so bulky?

And all of this is before encountering "Rabid" variants of these enemies, which I hear are a hundred times worse. Of course, this can all be mitigated very easily by playing in a group, which the game is practically SCREAMING for you to do, but if you choose to play this game solo, you have been warned. 7/10.

EDIT: Just encountered Rabid Stalkers, I am uninstalling.

This used to be one of my favorite games to play with friends. It used to work incredibly well. My friends could appear in my games at random to annoy me, and it was all in good fun.

That is no longer the case. With the ToS updates (which are their own controversy) have seemingly come some new backend changes that make it almost impossible to play with my friend. I wanted to show him the good gameplay, and fun writing of this game, but instead, we found hardlocks.

Changing network settings to switch from offline mode to friends only? The game hardlocks.
Booting up the game and trying to load the title screen? 25% chance the game hardlocks.
Attempt to join your friend through steam? 50% chance the game hardlocks.
Connection times out while trying to join your friend? The game hardlocks.
Friend has a minor internet hiccup? You get kicked back to the title screen, and the game hardlocks.
Got kicked back to the title screen and restarted the game to escape the hardlock? Well, you have to go into network settings and turn it back to online, which, of course, hardlocks, but at least it remembers you changed it.

We have spent more time trying to make the game work than actually playing it.

Not to mention another friend I played the game with a few years ago. The game encountered a crash, and for some reason this led to the game permanently blocking us from joining each other ever again. We tried everything to fix this reinstalling, forums, changing settings, blocking and unblocking. We even called gearbox support, who was unable to fix the issue after several hours. I miss playing with them.

It's sad to see what this game has become. It used to be such a straightforward good time.

I actually quite enjoye the first game and I was really hyped to play this one and surprisingly I hated almost every moment of this game and I really don't wan't to play the third title.  This game makes me want to rethink my stance as a completionist.

I had good luck as a Mordecai Sniper in the first game so I picked Zero and specced for Sniping in this title as well, but that is probably the absolute worst way to play for a number of reasons:

You scope out an area, slowly approach and pick people off methodically?  Well, the game only spawns most enemies once you're practically close enough for them to melee you.

You clear the room and want to move on to the objective?  Oh, well, I guess the devs thought it would be more fun if you just sat there an recleared the room that they refill over and over again.

Are you worried about having to walk back after dying?  No problems, the devs thought of that, too.  They'll just spawn you in the middle of the room you just cleared still full of the enemies who just murdered you.

Also, those enemies, the devs thought it would be SOOOOO FUN if they added some that took 10+ critical hits from your highest damage sniper rifle while being able to one-shot you instead.  After all, we need the NPCs to be having fun, too, right?  The devs make you fight multiple of those at a time in some cases.

It's almost as if the entire core gameplay is forcing you to do the same tedious reppetitive tasks on loop when there are so many better things you could be doing.  I disagree with how combat works at its very foundation in this title and it's the one consistent thing you have to deal with throughout.

And I'm really trying to like it.  I really am.  I kept thinking "maybe the build will come together in a few more levels.  Maybe if I just get this gun.  Maybe once I'm in the new game+." but it never gets better, it actually feels like it's getting less rewarding and more unfairly punishing as time goes on.

1/10 should never have purchased it even on sale.

Мне кажется, что меня нагло наебали. Все обзорщики заверяли, что игра шедевр. У игры очень положительные отзывы, и я действительно не понимаю почему.

Кратко о плюсах

Их практически нет за исключением разнообразия оружия и сочной стилистики игры. Оружия в игре реально много и оно очень сочное с огромным разнообразием способностей и характеристик. Лутер-шутер как никак. Стилистика на высоте. Игра выглядит шероховато намеренно, так, будто всех героев и всё окружение рисовали какой то черной ручкой или простым карандашом.

Минусы

Вся игра один сплошной минус! Игра приносит веселье первые четыре часа, а потом радость кончается. Локации однообразные и пустые, никакой живости мира тут нет, он максимально пустой, есть только три четыре территории, которые нужно зачистить, места для спавна автомобиля и все. У миров максимум отличаются цвета ландшафта и все. Враги-болванчики и боссы все как под копирку, никакого разнообразия. Персонажи максимально скучные и клишированные, интерес представляет лишь Красавчик Джек со своей харизмой и действительно интересным характером. В общем в игре нет абсолютно ничего, кроме однообразных боев в пустых мирах. Светлая память тем, кто решит закрыть данный дефектный продукт на 100%. Если мнение поменяется, поменяю обзор, но пока что игру продолжать не планирую, так как нет желания возвращаться в нее. Как по мне, Borderlands является слишком переоценённым продуктом. ♥♥♥♥♥ я вообще, тройку со всеми дополнениями купил, вдохновившись первыми 4 часами геймплея в двойку. As fun as Borderlands is, I feel that the Borderlands series personally had a few small issues. The navigation is fun at first, but sometimes can drag and become the worst part. The Pre-Sequel especially, which was a very fun game that was kind of plagued with a few navigation issues, and a lot of annoying back and forth.

Borderlands 2 does improve on the navigation, a little. However, I ran into several issues during my first returning playthrough that rubbed me the wrong way. Namely, which, Borderlands 2's PhysX implementation on PC, which is infamous to make loot disappear and cause many problems if on anything higher than Low.

And there were a little more than 'loot disappearing'. When this was set to high, it prevented the game from working past loading my save, at all. Setting it to 'Low' did fix the problem, however why this is even a problem is ridiculous.

I also ran into issues with the game difficulty being a bit high for my taste (I found myself going down a little more than I felt I should), as well as this being tenfold more apparent by minibosses I killed seemignly not remaining dead. Because lo and behold, I loaded my save after playing last night, struggled with the PhysX issue, then struggled with enemies being magically alive after having killed them the last time I was on.

Borderlands 2 is a fun game, however the issues it's plagued with made me not want to play anymore. And it's a shame, because Borderlands 2 is an amazing sequel to the original, and improves the original game in many ways.

Driving through purple water and taking double damage until you restart the game. General stuff that just added, seemingly at every level. Otherwise, I think the concepts were interesting. I didn't really enjoy having to look for a new gun to use just because mine were not good enough for the present task, but I suppose this is a feature of a looter and not a drawback. Overall, some things were not readily apparent either, such as how the leveling worked with the main storyline, as well as how things should be spent with the coins or tokens or whatnot. Story itself was mediocre, some of the characters were just very cliche but at the time this was released perhaps that was different. I am not sure what to make of it overall as there was definitely some fun to be had but it was a toilsome experience in many regards. I got it for free, and for that price obviously its worth a shot, but it came with bugs that cost me part of my sanity so perhaps it wasn't as free as I thought it was.
